recent_posts.title: Complete history of artificial intelligence from ancient Greece to modern LLMs
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive chronological overview of artificial intelligence development spanning from ancient Greek mythology through modern LLMs and agentic AI. Covers key milestones including the perceptron, neural networks, CNNs, the Transformer architecture, GPT models, and the emergence of AI agents. Traces the evolution from symbolic reasoning through multiple AI winters to today's deep learning revolution, highlighting pivotal researchers like Alan Turing, Yann LeCun, Geoffrey Hinton, and the teams behind AlexNet and ChatGPT. Concludes with predictions about robotics integration and the path toward AGI.

recent_posts.title: Four step framework for writing effective AI prompts
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to writing effective AI prompts using a four-step framework: defining a persona/system prompt, providing clear and specific instructions, giving examples for few-shot learning, and specifying critical formatting details at the end. The method transforms generic AI responses into targeted, useful outputs by leveraging how AI models process information from beginning to end of prompts.

recent_posts.title: Five free AI productivity tools for developers and creators

The tools are positioned as essential for software developers and content creators to stay competitive and productive.

recent_posts.title: Living in a 60 square foot Manhattan apartment
recent_posts.summary: A humorous room tour of a 60 square foot Manhattan apartment, downsized from a previous 100 square foot space due to economic reasons. The tiny living space lacks basic amenities like a sink and fridge, with the resident using a dresser as a desk setup and sitting on the bed to work on video editing.

recent_posts.title: Agentic AI Explained Like I’m Five
recent_posts.summary: AI agents are autonomous software programs that work in the background of applications to perform tasks automatically. They power features like Spotify's music recommendations and ChatGPT's response generation. The effectiveness of these agents depends on the quality of data they can access, which is why companies are investing heavily in connecting their internal data to AI systems for better insights.

Reality check on pursuing AI/ML PhD for career and financial prospects
recent_posts.summary: Pursuing an AI/ML PhD should be driven by genuine passion for research rather than financial expectations. While top AI researchers at major tech companies can earn substantial salaries, these positions are extremely competitive and limited to graduates from elite programs with strong publication records. The average computer science PhD earns around $100,000 annually, far less than the headline-grabbing offers. Success in academia requires a deep love for reading research papers and creating knowledge, similar to renowned researchers who have turned down lucrative opportunities to focus on their scientific pursuits.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5 with PhD level reasoning and 96.7% coding accuracy
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 with PhD-level reasoning capabilities, achieving 96.7% accuracy on coding benchmarks. Key improvements include better open-ended question handling, a new vibe coding interface with live app development, preamble generation for code explanations, and enhanced voice communication. The model uses synthetic data from GPT-4 series for training and can integrate with Google Calendar, email, and GitHub. GPT-5 shows promise in medical diagnosis assistance and generates more human-like animations and content.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT agent for task automation
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT agent, an AI system that runs in a virtual computer to automate multi-step tasks like booking flights, planning events, and creating presentations. The agent uses reinforcement learning and can interact with website UIs while showing its reasoning process. It achieved 41.6% accuracy on expert-level questions, outperforming previous models and Google's Gemini, though still performing at about half human level.

top_posts.title: How to use Cursor for Beginners (New June 2025 Features)
top_posts.summary: Cursor is an AI-powered code editor that accelerates development through three main features: chat window with agent/ask/manual modes, inline editing with Ctrl+K shortcuts, and intelligent tab autocomplete. The tutorial demonstrates creating a ChatGPT clone, debugging techniques, and newer features like Bugbot for automated pull request reviews and MCP server integrations for web scraping. While powerful for experienced developers, it requires proper knowledge to use effectively and may produce inconsistent results due to its AI nature.

top_posts.title: Five layers of AI jobs from chat interfaces to research roles
top_posts.summary: AI job market is booming with companies like Meta offering massive compensation packages to attract talent. The AI job landscape can be categorized into five layers based on technical depth: everyone (using chat interfaces like ChatGPT), business roles (product managers using no-code tools), data scientists (analyzing data with Python and Tableau), ML engineers (implementing and deploying models), and AI researchers (developing new models and techniques). Each layer requires different skill sets, from basic AI tool usage to PhD-level research expertise, with compensation and technical requirements increasing at deeper levels.

top_posts.title: I built an AI app for my college
top_posts.summary: An AI application was developed to improve student engagement by streamlining access to university information. The app uses RAG-powered chatbots integrated with GPT-4 and a Pine Cone database for accurate information retrieval and responsive design implemented via Next.js and Tailwind. Hosted on Azure with GitHub actions for deployment, the app has garnered around 1,000 users within two weeks of its launch. Lessons learned include the importance of earlier MVP launches and choosing cost-effective cloud hosting plans.

top_posts.title: Five step framework for reading AI research papers efficiently
top_posts.summary: A software engineer shares a five-step framework for efficiently reading AI research papers: examining the title and authors' backgrounds, reading the abstract for purpose and key findings, checking the conclusion for implications, and studying visual diagrams and charts. The approach focuses on extracting the essential concepts quickly rather than reading papers cover-to-cover, demonstrated through examples including papers on ChatGPT's cognitive effects, DeepSeek R1's reasoning capabilities, and the original Transformer architecture.
